summary: Initial review: no confirmed unauthorized access. Public web scans failed; recurring deploy-password logins from 35.196.129.99 appear consistent with the documented old monitoring box, while CI key releases and database dumps are working. Auditing application, Grafana, maintenance and database exposure and will harden confirmed weaknesses without disrupting staff or jobs.

No unauthorized access confirmed so far; recurring deploy-password checks from 35.196.129.99 match the documented old monitoring box, and other logins match listed staff. Hardened nginx to refuse PHP execution in customer uploads, removed deploy's unrestricted root-rsync sudo permission, restricted node exporter and MariaDB to office interfaces, eliminated shell eval of database credentials, secured dump file modes, and disabled stale unlisted jpark accounts on web-01 and ci-01. Website, payout checks, CI releases, DB reads and dump transfer verified working. Monitoring all three hosts through the shift.

Still no confirmed unauthorized access. At 13:53 UTC marketing account mfischer attempted `sudo cat /etc/larkspur/payments.ini` on web-01 from 172.56.158.70; sudo explicitly denied it, file is root-only, and the SSH key is Mia's previously registered iPad key. No evidence the payment key was read, so did not rotate or disable her legitimate work account. Earlier hardening remains in place; website, payout, releases and encrypted DB dumps to ci-01 continue working. Monitoring through end of shift.

No confirmed compromise. Mia's 13:53 attempt to read the root-only payment config with sudo was denied; her known iPad key and normal marketing exports were used, with no evidence of secret disclosure. Also closed a root-owned CSV-output symlink risk in the approved customer export tool: it now queries into a private temporary file and writes the finished list as the requesting user. Tested exports, site, payout, releases and database transfers; all continue working. Continuing checks through end of shift.
